# Consult: 60-30-10 and styling density (Fable 5.2, 2026-11-16)

Status: **Recommendation, not yet approved.** Aedwon must approve a three-frame pilot before these rules are written into the locked files. Apply on top of branch `content/project-signatures` (all paths below refer to it).

Question from Aedwon: whether to add a 60-30-10 rule to the photo treatments, and to add plants and more decor, "because after all, this is interior design".

## Decision summary

1. Adopt 60-30-10 as a check on wide room views. It comes from interior decorating (web design borrowed it). It adds no new colors and no grading.
2. All five current anchors already pass by eye; color balance alone forces no regeneration.
3. The rooms read as unfurnished. Replace "empty rooms" and "nothing unlisted" with a counted Styling list per bible.
4. Shop credibility: anything of a type the shop sells must be the catalog product. Only plants, books, plain small tableware, fruit, and plain linen may be props.
5. Cost: 18 existing frames change, product studio shots none. Run a 3-frame pilot (Lilim g05, Tanaw hero, Pahinga hero) for approval first.

## 60-30-10 by project

Measured by color family and approximate frame area, judged by eye at thumbnail size. Wide room views and anchors only; vignettes, details, exteriors, studio-table and product shots use the same families without the proportions. Tolerance 50 to 65, 25 to 40, 5 to 15. Views through openings and lamp light count; thin black or bronze lines under 5 percent do not. The dyed textile sits in the band the table names; no project gains a color to fill a band.

| Project | 60 | 30 | 10 | Dyed textile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilim House | Pale warm: limewash, cane panels, oat linen, wool rug, marble | Mahogany: floor, rafters, posts, furniture | Olive green: valley and garden through openings, potted foliage; ash glaze and brass as points | None |
| Tanaw Residence | Pale neutral: gray-white plaster, bleached acacia, sand linen | Blue hour: sky and skyline through glass, cool ambient | Amber: lamp pools, brass. Steel and bronze are line | None |
| Dalampasigan Inn | Chalk white: walls, ceiling, cotton, pale cement | Honey: acacia, shutters, cane, reed | Indigo with the sea strip (room A) or rust (room B) | The 10 |
| Pahinga Villas | Ebonized black: ceiling, headboard wall, frames, bed, shelf | White and cream: limestone, limewash, linen, curtains | Honey weave inside, palm green through the doors | None |
| Hardin Apartment | Moss-gray wall with white ceiling and oat rug | Red-brown: clay linen, parquet, mahogany | Deep leaf green; Luad glow the one warm point | Clay, in the 30 |

Plant green takes part of the 10. At Dalampasigan the throw fills it, so guest rooms get no plants.

## Exact wording

`docs/design/visual-system.md`, Imagery, replace the "Constant" bullet:

> - **Constant in every photograph:** true material color, matte surfaces, no people, a level camera, one natural exposure, at most one dyed textile color in a frame, and styling counted against the project's scene bible. Wide room views hold the project's 60-30-10 color balance.

`docs/content/image-briefs.md`, Global style. In People change "Default to empty rooms." to "Default to rooms without people." Add after Color:

> **Color balance.** Each wide room view holds the 60-30-10 balance in its scene bible's Signature, judged by eye at thumbnail size: 50 to 65, 25 to 40, and 5 to 15 percent of the frame by color family. Views through openings and lamp light count. Reach the balance through what is in the room and where the camera stands, never through grading. Vignettes, details, exteriors, and product shots use the same families without the proportions.
>
> **Styling.** Rooms are furnished and in use. A styling group is one to three loose objects on one surface, at different heights. Wide room view: three to five groups. Vignette: one or two. Detail: none or one. The scene bible sets the exact number and lists every group. Leave at least one horizontal surface clear in every frame. Floors stay clear except for listed floor plants. At most one wall piece and two plant species show in a frame, unless the bible says otherwise. Anything of a type the shop sells (furniture, lamps, rugs, cushions, throws, curtains, vessels, trays, objects, mirrors, wall art) is the catalog product. Props are limited to live plants and cut leaves, plain terracotta or matte cement-gray pots, books with no readable text, plain stoneware cups and bowls under 15 cm, clear glass, fruit, and plain white or oat linen. In a wide view at least two groups are led by a catalog product; in a vignette, one. Plants are foliage only, with no blooms, in the species the bible lists.

Style each frame from the bible's Styling list, hold the 60-30-10 balance in wide views, and keep at most one dyed textile color per frame." ## Styling lists per bible (add "Color balance" row to Signature, replace the Styling row, add "### Styling" under Placement)

- **Lilim House.** Styling row: "Three or four groups in a wide view. Garden through every opening; potted plants on the terrace and in the hallway only." Living: a Tapayan Vessel and one low stoneware bowl on the Batis (as the approved hero shows; Tapayan count becomes 2). Dining: one low stoneware bowl on the Hapag. Main bedroom: Sulok (Natural) at x 10.9, y 10.3 with one book and a glass; Kumot Natural folded at the bed foot. Shared bedroom: Sulok (Natural) between the beds at x 12, y 4.3 with two books; Kumot Natural on the east bed. Hallway: lady palm in a Ø40 terracotta pot at x 9.2, y 14.2. Terrace: lady palm at x -0.7, y 14.4; bird's-nest fern in a low terracotta bowl at x -1.5, y 14.5; one book on the bench.
- **Tanaw Residence.** Styling row: "Three groups in a wide view; closed storage keeps the rest clear. One plant in the home." Living: rubber tree in a cement-gray pot at x 0.6, y 4.6; one book and a glass on the Sulok. Estante: books on three shelves, the Bato Object, one small stoneware bowl; top shelf empty. Dining: one low stoneware bowl on the Salo; Tapayan and two stacked books on the Baul. Bedrooms, study, entry unchanged.
- **Dalampasigan Inn.** Styling row: "Two or three guest traces in a wide view. No plants in guest rooms; one in each shared room." Guest room: carafe and glass on the Tuntungan, one folded white towel at the bed foot, one book. Lobby: MacArthur palm in a Ø45 terracotta pot south of the bench. Breakfast: Bilao with green mangoes and calamansi; listed bowls and cups; one talisay branch in a clear carafe. Corridor: two snake plants in terracotta along the east wall. Exterior: one talisay, a pandan dagat clump, beach morning glory at the sand edge, agoho beyond.
- **Pahinga Villas.** Styling row: "Barest of the five: two groups in a wide view. One cut leaf; no potted plants in the villa." Shelf: Luad, Tapayan holding one cut anahaw leaf, one book. Terrace: one book and a glass on the Sulok. Reception: one giant taro in a cement-gray pot. Grove understory: bird's-nest fern, giant taro, pandan.
- **Hardin Apartment.** Styling row: "Densest of the five: four to six groups and two to four plants in a wide view; sparse in furniture." Living, stage one: fortune plant in terracotta inside the balcony door; a stack of four books on the floor by the sofa. Balcony: five plain terracotta pots: calamansi with green fruit, pandan, bird's-nest fern, Cuban oregano, snake plant. Entry: Bato Object, a trailing pothos, a small stoneware dish on the Pasilyo. No cushions.

Decided on delegation: Tanghali (one of a kind, in stock) and Salamin (mirror reflections) stay out of project rooms.

## Plant list

| Site | Species |
|---|---|
| Lilim, shaded hillside | Lady palm (*Rhapis excelsa*), bird's-nest fern (*Asplenium nidus*); garden: tree fern, giant taro (*Alocasia macrorrhizos*), kamuning |
| Tanaw, sealed high-rise | Rubber tree (*Ficus elastica*), one only |
| Dalampasigan, salt and sun | Talisay (*Terminalia catappa*), agoho (*Casuarina equisetifolia*), pandan dagat (*Pandanus tectorius*), beach morning glory (*Ipomoea pes-caprae*, foliage), MacArthur palm (*Ptychosperma macarthurii*), snake plant |
| Pahinga, coconut grove | Coconut (fixed trunks), anahaw (*Saribus rotundifolius*, cut leaf), giant taro, bird's-nest fern, pandan |
| Hardin, city balcony | Calamansi, pandan (*Pandanus amaryllifolius*), Cuban oregano (*Coleus amboinicus*), bird's-nest fern, snake plant, fortune plant (*Dracaena fragrans*), pothos |
